SOURCE EXTRACT — read from the full djvu text, 2026-09-06 (p_433)

YEAR BOOK OF THE YOUNG MEN'S CHRISTIAN ASSOCIATIONS OF NORTH AMERICA
Internet Archive: yearbookyoungme01commgoog — NOT lending-restricted, djvu text 1,095,671 bytes

TWO VOLUMES ARE BOUND IN THIS ONE ITEM, AND THE CATALOGUE ONLY NAMES ONE
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Internet Archive metadata gives `year: 1899, date: 1899`. The scan contains TWO complete annual
volumes:

    scan line    107  "YEAR BOOK ... For the Year 1899."
    scan line  67857  "YEAR BOOK ... For the Year 1900."

Both years are read off the volumes' own title pages. So this single item fills TWO of the years
in the project's 1898-1905 hole, and a reader who trusted the catalogue field would have taken
only one. (The line at 67857+397 reading "FOR THE YEAR 1899." sits inside the 1900 volume and is
a retrospective statistics heading, not a second title page.)

For working purposes: lines 1-67820 are the 1899 volume, 67821-end the 1900 volume.


I. THE MONTREAL ASSOCIATION'S PAID STAFF, 1899
==============================================
The branch-by-branch directory, Quebec section (scan line 16796 onwards), quoted with the OCR's
own slips left where they fall:

    Quebec*

Read against the alphabetical list (below), which is set in cleaner type, that is:

    General Secretary        D. A. BUDGE
    Assistant                C. K. CALHOUN
    Assistant                JOHN ROY
    Educational Director     E. G. RANDAL
    Physical Director        W. H. BALL, JR.
    Junior Department        F. A. CROWE
    Railroad Department      F. S. MORRISON
    (McGill University)      A. H. GRACE

II. THE SAME MEN IN THE ALPHABETICAL LIST, WITH THEIR YEARS OF ENTRY
====================================================================
The list is headed "General Secretaries and Other Paid Officers in Alphabetical Order.
APRIL 1, 1899." and carries its own legend, printed above it:

    "The figures after each name indicate the year of entry into Association work."
    "The men whose names are marked thus * have taken a course of instruction in one of the
     [training schools]"

The Montreal entries (scan lines 19651-20666), verbatim:

    *BiUl, W. H., Montreal. Ph. Dir., 89          [= BALL — see the note below]
    BudK«>. D- A., Montreal. Set;., 74            [= BUDGE, Sec., 74]
    Calhoun, C. K.. Montreal, Asst., 90
    Crowe. F. A., Montreal, Asst., 94
    Grace, A. H., McGiU Univ., Montreal Sec, 97
    Morrison, F S., Montreal RR. Sec, 93
    ♦Randal E. G., Montreal Ed. Dir., 93
    Roy, John, Montreal, Asst., 99

So, dated:
    W. H. BALL, JR.   Physical Director   entered Association work 1889   *training school
    D. A. BUDGE       General Secretary   entered 1874
    C. K. CALHOUN     Assistant           entered 1890
    F. A. CROWE       Assistant           entered 1894
    A. H. GRACE       Secretary, McGill   entered 1897
    F. S. MORRISON    Railroad Secretary  entered 1893
    E. G. RANDAL      Educational Dir.    entered 1893   *training school
    JOHN ROY          Assistant           entered 1899

WHY "BiUl" IS BALL AND NOT BILL, settled on the page rather than by preference. The entry sits
in an alphabetical list between

    Ball. W. D., Los Angeles, Cal„ Sec., 90
    *BiUl, W. H., Montreal. Ph. Dir., 89
    Ballaiitine,W.G., Springfield, Mass.,Tr.Sch.97

— i.e. between Ball, W. D. and Ballantine. A name spelled Bill would sort roughly two hundred
entries later. It is Ball. The branch directory at line 16803 prints it cleanly as
"Phy§. Director, W. H. Ball, Jr." in any case; the two agree.


III. WHAT IS NEW HERE AND WHAT ALREADY EXISTED
==============================================
Checked by grep against the repo before being written down.

  NEW — the year. This project held the Year Book for 1891-1897, 1906-1908, 1921 and 1922. It did
    not hold 1899 or 1900. Two years of the 1898-1905 hole are now filled.

  NEW — E. G. RANDAL, Educational Director of the Montreal association, in Association work since
    1893 and a training-school man. The name occurs nowhere in this project. It is the earliest
    Educational Director the project has by nearly twenty years: the next is F. H. Spinney, from
    about 1917.

  NEW as a date — JOHN ROY. The name is on the directors-index sweep list as an unswept camp
    name. Here he is an Assistant at the Montreal association who ENTERED ASSOCIATION WORK IN
    1899, i.e. he is new in post in this volume. Whether this John Roy is the John Roy on the
    camp's own boards is NOT established and must not be assumed from the name alone.

  NEW as a date — A. H. GRACE at McGill University, entered 1897.

  ALREADY HELD — "W. H. Ball, Jr." with the Jr., which the 1893-1897 volumes print in all five
    (see f_4966 and the roster table in wiki/people/directors-index.md). What 1899 adds is that
    HE IS STILL PHYSICAL DIRECTOR IN 1899, five years after founding the camp and one year after
    the annual report has him running the 1898 senior camp, and that HIS YEAR OF ENTRY INTO
    ASSOCIATION WORK IS 1889, which this project did not have. By the 1906 volume the Physical
    Director is J. E. Merritt, so Ball leaves the post somewhere in 1900-1905.

  ALREADY HELD — Budge and Calhoun.


IV. THE 1900 VOLUME — AND A CORRECTION MADE THE SAME HOUR
=========================================================
[SUPERSEDED 2026-09-06, within the hour of writing it. This section was headed "THE 1900 VOLUME:
PRESENT, READ, AND MOSTLY UNREADABLE" and concluded: "THE HONEST STATEMENT: the 1900 Montreal
roster HAS NOT BEEN READ. The OCR of that half of the scan is too degraded to read a roster off,
and its silence about Ball is a fact about the scanner, NOT evidence that he had left. Whether
Ball is in the 1900 volume is UNKNOWN. The item is not lending-restricted, so the page images are
fetchable and would settle it; that has not been done."

THAT WAS WRONG, AND THE WAY IT WAS WRONG IS THE POINT. The Year Book lists the same staff TWICE:
an ALPHABETICAL LIST of paid officers, and a BRANCH DIRECTORY arranged by city. Only the
alphabetical list is degraded in the 1900 half. The branch directory reads about as well as the
1899 one — and it had not been looked at. The volume was searched in one section, the section
came back unreadable, and the result was written up as a fact about the volume. That is the same
failure as reading a source for one thing and recording it as read: A SOURCE SEARCHED IN ONE
SECTION IS SEARCHED IN ONE SECTION. No page images were needed and none were fetched.]

THE MONTREAL ROSTER FOR 1900, from the Quebec branch directory (scan line 76651 of the item,
8830 of the 1900 half), quoted with the OCR's slips left in:

    <|aebec.
    Montreal                     D A. Budge
        Asst.,                   C. K. Calhoun
        Asst,                    F. E. Buruess
        " Asst.,                 John Hoy
        Phys. Director,          W. H. Ball. Jr.

    McGill University....
    Quebec                       H. H. Distin
        " Phys. Director,        RoHert Aiken
    Sherbrooke                   J. H. Bryce

Read against the 1899 volume, that is:

    General Secretary        D. A. BUDGE
    Assistant                C. K. CALHOUN
    Assistant                F. E. BURNESS      [see the note on this name below]
    Assistant                JOHN ROY           ["John Hoy" — H for R]
    Physical Director        W. H. BALL, JR.
    Junior Department        — printed, with no name against it
    Railroad Department      F. S. MORRISON
    McGill University        — printed, with no name against it
    (no Educational Director line at all)

FOUR CHANGES FROM 1899, and each one is read off the directory itself rather than inferred:

  W. H. BALL, JR. IS STILL PHYSICAL DIRECTOR. His departure from the post is therefore bounded to
    1901-1905, not 1900-1905 — the 1906 volume has J. E. Merritt in it.

  E. G. RANDAL IS GONE, and Montreal has NO Educational Director line whatever in 1900. So his
    tenure is bounded to at most 1893-1899, and the post lapsed after him rather than passing to
    someone else.

  F. A. CROWE IS GONE from the Junior Department, whose line is printed with nothing against it.

  A. H. GRACE IS GONE from McGill University, likewise printed blank.

  AND ONE ADDITION: an assistant the directory gives as "F. E. Buruess" and the alphabetical list
    gives as "Burgeoii, F. B., Montreal, Ant., 99". The two disagree on the initials AND on the
    surname, and neither is legible enough to settle. Burness? Burgess? Bourgeois? What is certain
    is that Montreal gained an assistant who entered Association work in 1899. The name is left
    unresolved here rather than picked.

A LEAD, AND DELIBERATELY NOT AN IDENTIFICATION. The same 1900 volume lists a Randal, initials
rendered "E. O.", as secretary of an association whose city the OCR gives as "TaustoD" —
plausibly TAUNTON, MASSACHUSETTS, though the city names around it ("Dalnlh" for Duluth) are not
in an order that confirms a state grouping. Whether this is Montreal's E. G. Randal in a new post
is NOT established, and the initials do not match cleanly. It is written down because a man who
appears in this project for the first time today, and vanishes from Montreal after one recorded
year, is worth a thread; it is not written down as his next job.

V. "KANAWANA" OCCURS ZERO TIMES IN EITHER VOLUME
================================================
So do "summer camp" and "camping". The three hits on "boys' camp" are elsewhere in North America.
The single "camp" occurring near Montreal or Quebec is "winter campaign work". This is the same
result the 1921 volume gave and for the same reason: the Year Book rosters ASSOCIATIONS AND THEIR
PAID STAFF, not their programmes. A camp does not appear in it even when the association running
the camp does.


VI. A TOOLING FINDING THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THIS VOLUME
========================================================
This item was found only because the enumeration was re-run on a TITLE rather than an identifier
stem. `identifier:ymcayearbookoffi*` returns three items. A title query returns nine under that
title and four more under a second title the series also used, "Year Book of the Young Men's
Christian Associations of North America" — which is where the 1899/1900 item lives. It was never
reachable from the stem the earlier sweep used. (Rule 16: an enumeration is only as wide as the
string it was run on.)

AND, SERIOUSLY: THE INTERNET ARCHIVE SCRAPE ENDPOINT SERVED STALE RESULTS FOR A DIFFERENT QUERY.
`https://archive.org/services/search/v1/scrape` was observed, repeatedly and reproducibly on
2026-09-06, returning the result set of a PREVIOUS query while reporting it as the answer to the
current one — `identifier:ymcayearbookoffi*` returned eleven items, all of them volumes of The
School magazine from an enumeration run minutes earlier. A quoted, non-wildcard query for a
single known identifier returned the same eleven. Two further traps on the same endpoint: adding
`year` to the `fields` list returns ITEMS UNRELATED TO THE QUERY ("Scream In The Night",
"Scrooge"), and adding `date` returns zero.

An enumeration that silently answers a question you did not ask is worse than one that fails.
USE `https://archive.org/advancedsearch.php?q=...&fl[]=identifier&fl[]=title&rows=N&page=1&output=json`
INSTEAD — it was tested against the same queries and returned correct, query-specific results
every time. (A claim was made earlier in this session's working notes that advancedsearch returns
HTML rather than JSON, which is why the scrape endpoint was used at all. That claim was wrong and
never reached the repo: advancedsearch returns JSON when `output=json` is set, and the parameter
had been omitted. This project has used it successfully before — see the Green Triangle
enumeration.) A helper is at the scratchpad's `ias.py`.

QUERIES RUN: title:("official rosters") AND title:("year book"); title:("year book of the young
men's christian associations"); title:("young men's christian associations of north america") AND
title:("year book"); title:("year book") AND title:("christian associations");
identifier:ymcayearbookoffi*; and archive.org/metadata/<id> on each of the eleven items found.
